item.title: Implement safe_extract.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator instruction: Implement `safe_extract.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work.

Context: this is a security-sensitive extraction module, so validate every path and member at the boundary, fail visibly with the specified errors, and never silently skip or clamp unsafe input. Keep functions under 60 lines, add meaningful assertions at boundaries, and avoid unnecessary abstraction. Commit the work on the item's branch; do not push.

reasons: sizer: critical -> x_high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier

model_reasons.implement: Security-sensitive extraction logic; medium is the configured maximum effort, and strict review backs it up. Claude-code quota is tight, so no extra stages.

Implemented safe_extract.extract per SPEC.md on branch archon/maeqn6y2-implement-safe-extract-py-per-spec-md-wi. Commits e9a6bfc (implementation and 36 focused unittest tests) and af55daa (removed a tautological assert). Head af55daa, tree 769a8b6. Before: both existing tests error with NotImplementedError. Now: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -W error -m unittest` runs 36 tests, all OK, run by me on the final head. The whole batch is validated (entry shape, names, bytes, duplicate and file/directory collisions, root and every target via lstat) before any write; files use exclusive mode, so nothing is overwritten or link-followed. Not verified: three of four reviewers could not run git or unittest in their sandbox, so their reviews are read-only. Open follow-ups, all non-blocking: os.path.abspath normalises '..' lexically before the root check; on case-insensitive filesystems 'A' and 'a' in one batch can raise FileExistsError mid-write (spec is silent on case); the unencodable-name test does not isolate the explicit encode check; no test asserts names are not normalised. Two production asserts remain, which python -O strips. Still running: nothing started by me; reviewer processes will stop when this stage ends. Review: 4 reviewers delegated. pr.body: Approach: extract() validates the root (lstat, real directory), every entry (tuple of (str, bytes), name rules), batch name collisions in either order, and every target path (lstat each component; no symlink or non-directory ancestor; target absent). Only then does it write, using open(path, 'xb') so existing files and links are never overwritten or followed. Parents are created with makedirs(exist_ok=True). Key files: safe_extract.py, test_safe_extract.py. Checks: unittest, 36 tests OK on af55daa. Assumptions: entries must be tuples (lists rejected); root is abspath-normalised before checks; name encoding must be valid UTF-8. Limits: case-insensitive filesystems may raise FileExistsError mid-batch; the reviewers' sandboxes could not run git or tests, so their reviews are read-only.
pr.summary: Made safe extraction work per SPEC.md. Now: extract validates the whole batch before any write and refuses symlinks, overwrites and collisions. Before: stub raising NotImplementedError; now: 36 unit tests pass.
pr.title: Implement safe_extract.extract per SPEC.md

risk.why: Security-sensitive module that creates files and directories from untrusted names; it must reject symlinks, overwrites and traversal. Review by R1 confirmed high.
